$description: NL's design tokens, in the W3C Design Tokens Community Group format 2025.10. This file is the one source for every UI: the build generates from it (web/tokens) the CSS custom properties and TypeScript constants of the web code and the Dart tokens of apps/client, and the generated files are never committed. `palette` holds primitives that the generator never emits. `theme` holds the color themes, each in a light and a dark mode with the same semantic tokens. Every other group is the same in every theme and mode. Rules: docs/design/ui.md, sections 3 and 11.

palette.$description: Primitive values that the themes share. The generator emits none of them, so screens can only use the semantic tokens of a theme. A color's name is its approximate OKLCH lightness times 100.

red.$description: Destructive actions and failures, and nothing else.

yellow.$description: Warnings, always shown together with an icon.

orange.$description: Reserved for "microphone on" (product rule 8), on every end, LEDs included. No other token may use this hue.

shadow.$description: The shadows of each mode. Shadows exist only on floating layers; surfaces in the page are flat.

theme.$description: The color themes the user chooses from (docs/design/ui.md, section 3). Each theme has a light and a dark mode, and every theme and mode holds the same tokens; the first theme is the default. Descriptions are given once, in the default theme's light mode. Danger, warning, and the reserved microphone hue are the same in every theme.

sea.$description: Sea salt, the default: cool neutrals and an azure accent that suits the default character's blue hair.

app.$description: The window background behind the conversation and most screens.

sidebar.$description: The sidebar and other secondary panes.

raised.$description: Cards that sit on the app surface: approvals, tasks, the composer.

sunken.$description: Wells inside a surface: code blocks, tool input and output previews.

overlay.$description: Floating layers: menus, popovers, sheets, the detail panel when it floats. Pair with a shadow.

inverse.$description: Tooltips and other small inverted layers.

secondary.$description: Working text in the full view, metadata, secondary labels.

tertiary.$description: Timestamps, placeholders, hints. Still meets 4.5:1 on every surface.

disabled.$description: Disabled controls. Exempt from contrast rules, so never use it for text that matters.

strong.$description: Borders that identify a control on their own (checkboxes, switches). Meets 3:1 on every surface.

hover.$description: Overlay drawn over any surface when the pointer is over an interactive element.

pressed.$description: Overlay drawn while an interactive element is pressed.

selected.$description: Overlay for the selected item of a list, such as the open conversation in the sidebar.

focus.$description: Keyboard focus ring. Meets 3:1 on every surface and bubble.

fill.$description: Primary buttons. Neutral on purpose: color belongs to the character, not to the interface.

on-fill.$description: Text and icons on a primary button.

accent.$description: The slot a character pack fills at run time, after checking its contrast and its distance from the reserved hue. These values belong to the placeholder character.

fill.$description: Accent fill, such as the character's avatar ring and the working indicator.

on-fill.$description: Text and icons on the accent fill.

soft.$description: Tint behind the character's message bubbles.

text.$description: Accent used as text or an icon on surfaces and on the soft tint.

character.$description: The character's message bubbles (the message tool, M5).

on-fill.$description: Text and icons on a destructive button.

soft.$description: Background of a failed tool row or an error tip.

icon.$description: Warning icons. A warning always has an icon, never color alone.

fill.$description: The reserved "microphone on" hue, for the listening dot and ring. It is below 4.5:1 on light surfaces, so a label beside it stays in ink.

scrim.$description: Dims what is behind a modal sheet or dialog.

sheet.$description: Sheets, dialogs, and the floating detail panel.

pet-bubble.$description: The pet's message bubbles, which float over any wallpaper.

sakura.$description: Sakura: warm neutrals and a rose accent.

matcha.$description: Matcha: green-gray neutrals and a green accent.

lavender.$description: Lavender: violet-gray neutrals and a violet accent.

graphite.$description: Graphite: gray neutrals, with ink as the accent.

family.$description: System font stacks; NL bundles no font. The `flutter` extension lists the families the Flutter app asks for instead, in order; an empty list means the platform's default font.

sans.$description: Interface and message text: the platform's UI font for Latin, then Chinese fonts, then emoji.

mono.$description: Tool input and output, and code.

weight.$description: Chinese text looks heavy above 600, so nothing is bolder.

line-height.$description: Multipliers of the font size. Body text is generous for Chinese.

type.$description: Text styles. Screens use these rather than the font tokens above.

display.$description: The largest heading, for first-run screens.

body.$description: Messages, working text, and other reading text.

ui.$description: Labels, rows, menus, and the sidebar.

code.$description: Tool input and output, and code blocks.

space.$description: Spacing on a 4 px grid. The name is the multiple of 4 px.

sm.$description: Chips, inline code, and small tags.

md.$description: Buttons, inputs, menu items, and tool rows.

offset.$description: Gap between an element and its focus ring.

sm.$description: Compact controls in rows and toolbars.

touch-target.$description: The smallest area a finger can hit reliably, on the phone and the pet.

lg.$description: The character screen and the first run.

detail-width.$description: The detail panel when it sits beside the conversation.

reading-width.$description: The widest a conversation column grows, for comfortable line lengths.

titlebar-height.$description: The least height of the desktop window's title bar. On Windows it grows to the height of the system's caption buttons.

breakpoint.$description: Window widths where the desktop layout changes. The main window is at least 480 px wide.

medium.$description: Below this the sidebar becomes a drawer.

wide.$description: From this width the detail panel sits beside the conversation instead of over it.

motion.$description: Interface motion: short, easing out, never bouncing. With reduced motion on, the generated CSS sets every duration to 0. Character motion belongs to the renderer, not to these tokens.

base.$description: Expanding rows, opening menus and popovers.

out.$description: Things entering or changing: fast start, gentle stop.

in-out.$description: Things moving from one place on screen to another.

character.$description: The default avatar that web/stage and the apps draw (UI design note, section 10): a jelly-like ball in bright sea blue, flat and 2D, with a glossy highlight, pink cheeks, and two white upright bars for eyes. Its colors are the same in every theme and mode; an avatar the user chooses, or a character pack, brings its own.

body.$description: The ball. Flat shading: the lit body, set a little up and to the left, leaves a rim of body-shade at the lower right.

shine.$description: The glossy highlight on the ball, and the sparkle when it smiles.

blush.$description: The cheeks, rosier when it smiles or waits for an OK.

eye.$description: The eyes: two upright bars, ^ ^ when it smiles, > < when squished. On a device's small screen they are the whole face.

bubble.$description: The small bubble that holds a glyph (thinking dots, a question mark, sleep); white so that it reads on any wallpaper.

mic.$description: The listening ring, in the reserved "microphone on" hue (product rule 8).
